examples.en: I added cinnamon to the pie.
Kids love the crust of fresh bread.
A pine tree has thick bark.

related.en: cinnamon — the spice
crust, rind — of bread, cheese, a lemon
bark — of a tree; also the cortex in anatomy

examples.en: You can't use your phone during the lesson.
The train arrived on time.

related.en: during — a preposition, followed by the genitive
on time, without being late

note: Two words is a preposition with a noun (во вре́мя обе́да), one word is an adverb meaning «on time». In speech the stress tells them apart.

examples.en: A thunderstorm is forecast for tonight.
Thunder is rumbling in the distance.
Lightning struck a tree.

related.en: thunderstorm — a storm with thunder and lightning
thunder — the sound only
lightning — the flash

examples.en: My uncle told a funny joke.
Don't be offended, it was just a joke.

related.en: joke — a short funny story with a punchline, told to entertain
joke, jest — something said or done for fun

note: Not an «anecdote»: анекдо́т is a told joke. A true story about an event is «забавная исто́рия».

examples.en: We have fast internet at home.
Don't be so sly, tell me honestly!

related.en: fast, quick — бы́стрый по́езд
cunning, sly — хи́трый торгове́ц

examples.en: You play the guitar really well!
Hey, Seryoga! How's it going?

related.en: great, excellent; very (colloq.) — здо́рово получи́лось
hi, hey (colloq., among friends) — Здорово́, друг!

note: Only the stress tells these words apart. Здорово́ is a greeting between close people; to older people say «здра́вствуйте».

examples.en: The pharmacy is open around the clock.

examples.ru: Поезд идёт до Москвы почти двое [су́ток].
examples.en: The train takes almost two days and nights to get to Moscow.
In winter the day is short and the night is long.

related.en: a 24-hour period, day and night together — круглые су́тки
day, the daylight part; also a calendar day — день рожде́ния

note: Су́тки has only a plural: двое су́ток, пять су́ток. English has no single word for it: «24 hours» is the closest.

examples.en: We need some rest in the fresh air.
He took his vacation in August.
The children's winter break has started.
I have a day off on Saturday.

related.en: rest, relaxation in general — хоро́ший о́тдых
vacation, leave from work — уйти́ в о́тпуск
school or university break — зи́мние кани́кулы
day off from work — рабо́тать без выходны́х

note: Кани́кулы has no singular. «On break» is «на кани́кулах».

examples.en: He raised his glass to our health.
Put the carafe of water on the table.
There's a little compote left in the pitcher.

related.en: stemmed glass, wine glass — бока́л вина
carafe, a glass bottle with a stopper for water or juice — графи́н воды
pitcher, jug with a handle — кувши́н молока

examples.en: He fell and bruised his buttocks.
Models often have high cheekbones.
The girl has rosy cheeks.

related.en: buttocks, bottom — plural only
cheekbones — высо́кие ску́лы
cheeks — румя́ные щёки

examples.en: We got very tired after the hike.
Tomorrow I have to get up at six.

related.en: to get tired — уста́ть от рабо́ты; impf. устава́ть
to get up, stand up — вста́ть ра́но; impf. встава́ть

note: Уста́ть means «to get tired»: я уста́л is «I'm tired».

examples.en: They say a ghost lives in this house.
A ghost appeared in the castle at night.
The team has not lost its fighting spirit.

related.en: spirit — inner strength, morale — боево́й дух
ghost, apparition — привиде́ние в до́ме
ghost, specter; also figurative — при́зрак войны́

examples.en: We'll be there soon.
I've almost finished the report.
I got back from vacation recently.

related.en: soon, shortly — ско́ро уви́димся
almost, nearly — почти́ гото́в
recently, not long ago — неда́вно ви́дел

examples.en: I don't know this man.
- Are you hungry? - No, thank you.
I don't have time.

related.en: not — before a verb, adjective or adverb — я не рабо́таю
no (as an answer); there is no, I have no — у меня́ нет сестры́

note: Before a verb use only «не» (я не рабо́таю). «Нет» is the answer «no» and also «there is no / I have no». Wrong: «я нет работаю», «у меня не сестры».

examples.en: I bought new fins for diving.
Swallows fly back to us in spring.

related.en: flipper, fin (of a diver, seal, penguin) — ла́сты для плавания
swallow, the bird — ла́сточка в небе

note: Ла́сточка is also a term of endearment: «ла́сточка моя́».

examples.en: A button came off the shirt.
Press the doorbell button.

related.en: button on clothing — пришить пу́говицу
push button, one you press — of a doorbell, elevator, phone, appliance

note: Кно́пка is also a snap fastener on a jacket or pillowcase.

meanings: eraser or rubber band: ластик or резинка?

examples.en: I erased the mistake with an eraser.
I tie my hair in a ponytail with a hair tie.

related.en: eraser, for rubbing out pencil — купить ла́стик и каранда́ш
elastic band, hair tie, rubber band — рези́нка для воло́с, канцеля́рская рези́нка

note: In speech рези́нка can also mean an eraser, so you will be understood. But a hair tie is never «ла́стик».

examples.en: The glasses are in the case.
Buy a case for your phone.

related.en: case, a hard box or holder shaped to the object — for glasses, a violin
cover, a soft slip-on case — for a phone, furniture, a car seat

note: A gun holster is «ко́бура».

meanings: cake: калач, торт, пирожное or пирог?

examples.en: Mom baked a cake for my birthday.
Pastries were served with tea.
Grandma is baking an apple pie.

examples.ru: В городе до сих пор пекут [калачи́].
examples.en: They still bake kalachi in the town, a white bread of a traditional shape.

related.en: cake — a large cake, for a birthday or celebration
pastry — an individual small cake, e.g. an eclair — пиро́жное с кре́мом
pie — baked dough with a filling, sweet or savory
kalach — a traditional white wheat bread of a special shape, not a sweet cake

note: Cookies and biscuits are «пече́нье», and a small filled bun is «пирожо́к».

examples.en: He dreams of fame as an actor.
It's Nina's name day today.
They invited all their relatives to the christening.

related.en: fame, glory — a reputation, not a celebration
name day — the feast day of the saint whose name you bear, celebrated by the individual
christening, baptism — the celebration for a baptized child

examples.en: I need a thread and a needle.
The dentist recommends using dental floss.
The film is coming to an end.

related.en: end — коне́ц фильма; not a thread
thread, for sewing — ни́тка с игло́й
thread, filament — зубная нить (floss), нить жаро́вки, нить расска́за (the thread of a story)

examples.ru: Напиши на конверте [и́ндекс], без него письмо задержится.
examples.en: Write the postal code on the envelope, or the letter will be delayed.
The student put his record book on the table.

related.en: postal code, ZIP code; also a numerical indicator, e.g. a price index
student record book (colloq. for зачётная книжка)

skip: pure false-friend article: Serbian погоди means 'guess', Russian погоди́ means 'wait'; no point for an English speaker

examples.ru: На ферме у них три [ло́шади] и две коровы.
examples.en: They have three horses and two cows on the farm.
A white horse raced across the field.
This mare will foal soon.

related.en: horse — the general, ordinary word for either sex
steed, horse — as a riding animal; poetic; also the chess knight (шахматный конь)
mare — female only

note: In everyday speech «horse» is usually ло́шадь; конь sounds more elevated.

examples.en: Why did you buy so much bread?
Why didn't you come yesterday?

related.en: why, what for — asks about a purpose
why, for what reason — asks about a cause

note: English «why» covers both. If you could ask «what for?», use заче́м; the answer goes with что́бы. If you ask «for what reason?», use почему́; the answer goes with потому́ что.

examples.en: I did nothing all day.
I have nothing to wear tonight.
There's nothing to eat in the fridge.

related.en: nothing — goes with не and a finite verb
nothing to (do, eat, wear) — goes with an infinitive

note: The stress differs: ничего́, but не́чего. «I'm not reading anything» is я ничего́ не чита́ю, while «I have nothing to read» is мне не́чего чита́ть.

examples.en: The weather is nice today.
What a pretty hairstyle she has!
Have a nice day!

related.en: beautiful, pretty — pleasing to the eye or ear: a face, a dress, a city, a song
good, nice — pleasant, favorable: weather, a day, news, a vacation

note: English «nice» often matches хоро́ший, not краси́вый: nice weather is хоро́шая пого́да, a nice day is хоро́ший день, and «to ask nicely» is хорошо́ попроси́ть.

examples.en: We danced until morning yesterday.
The children are dancing around the Christmas tree.

related.en: to dance — neutral, any dance (waltz, tango)
to dance — colloquial, a folk or lively dance

note: Two verbs for «to dance». They also differ in form: я танцу́ю, but я пляшу́, ты пля́шешь.

examples.en: I eat everything except fish.
These pills are for a headache.

related.en: except, apart from — introduces the exception: все, кроме Ани
from; for, against — where something comes from or what it protects against: письмо от брата, лекарство от кашля

note: Only кро́ме introduces an exception. Both prepositions take the genitive.

examples.en: My name is Igor.
They named their daughter Anna.
What is this street called?

related.en: to call: меня зовут - my name is (for people and pets); звать в гости - to invite
to name, give a name: называть сына Антоном (instr.)
to be called, for things and places: a cafe, a film, a book

note: A person's name stays in the nominative: меня зовут Мария. After назвать the name is in the instrumental: назвали Марией. For things never «зову́т», only называ́ется.

examples.en: In winter I wear a warm hat.
On the beach she put on a wide-brimmed hat.
He bought a new cap for running.

related.en: winter hat — knitted or fur; the шапка-ушанка has ear flaps
hat, usually with a brim
cap with a visor, a summer cap

note: The шапка-уша́нка has «ears» («уши») that fold down in the cold.

examples.en: He speaks Russian with a slight accent.

examples.ru: В этом слове [ударе́ние] падает на первый слог.
examples.en: In this word the stress falls on the first syllable.

related.en: accent — a foreign accent in pronunciation: говорить с акцентом; also emphasis: сделать акцент на чём-то
stress — the stressed syllable of a word: поставить ударение

note: Stress is «placed» in Russian: поста́вьте ударе́ние.

examples.en: Our professor gives lectures at the university.

examples.ru: Мой [учи́тель] русского языка вышел на пенсию.
examples.en: My Russian teacher has retired.
She works as a lecturer at the institute.

related.en: professor — a university rank, a senior title
teacher in a primary or secondary school
instructor, lecturer — at a college, an institute or a course

note: Профе́ссор is only a high university rank, not a school teacher. A school teacher is учи́тель and is addressed by first name and patronymic.

examples.ru: Вчера мы посмотрели весь [сериа́л] за вечер.
examples.en: Yesterday we watched the whole series in one evening.
I liked the last episode.

related.en: TV series as a whole, with all its episodes (masc.)
one episode; also a set: серия марок (fem.)

note: A сериа́л consists of many се́рий: в сериа́ле мно́го се́рий.

examples.en: I add a spoonful of sour cream to the borscht.
She poured cream into her coffee.

related.en: sour cream — with borscht, dumplings, pelmeni
cream (sweet) — for coffee and for whipping (plural only)

note: Whipped cream is «взби́тые сли́вки». Сли́вки exists only in the plural.

examples.en: After lunch I wash the dishes.
Pour the water into a plastic container.
Blood flows through the blood vessels.

related.en: dishes, tableware as a whole: plates, cups, pots (singular only)
container — one vessel for liquid, tank
vessel — in formal style and in anatomy: кровено́сный сосу́д

note: Посу́да means «dishes» as a whole. One dish or container is not посу́да but ёмкость, or colloquially посу́дина.

examples.ru: На [у́треннике] в саду дети читали стихи.
examples.en: At the kindergarten party the children recited poems.
The teacher wrote a remark in the school diary.
Leave the night light on, the child is afraid of the dark.

related.en: children's party at kindergarten or school — not a morning
diary; also a pupil's school notebook for homework and grades
night light, a small lamp that stays on at night — not the night

note: The roots look familiar, but do not guess the meaning from у́тро, день, ночь.

examples.en: Uncle Vitya is my godfather.

examples.ru: Лучшая подруга станет [свиде́тельницей] на нашей свадьбе.
examples.en: My best friend will be our witness at the wedding.

related.en: godfather (godmother: крёстная) — holds the child at the baptism
wedding witness (female: свиде́тельница) — signs the marriage register

examples.ru: Мы зашли в [собо́р] и поставили свечи.
examples.en: We went into the cathedral and lit candles.
Tomorrow there's a parents' meeting at school.

related.en: cathedral, a large church (Исаа́киевский собо́р); also a church council
meeting, assembly — of a building's residents, of a school

examples.ru: Купи мне [любо́й] хлеб, мне всё равно.
examples.en: Buy me any bread, I don't care which.
Every day he walks the dog.
This store sells all sorts of toys.

related.en: any, whichever — one by free choice: любо́й день
all kinds of, various (mostly plural): вся́кие книги
each, every — individually, one by one: ка́ждый ребёнок

note: Trap: вся́кие игрушки is not «all toys» but «all sorts of toys». For «every», use ка́ждый; вся́кий in the singular (вся́кий зна́ет) sounds bookish.

examples.en: I left my gloves at home, my hands are freezing.
Grandma knitted me warm mittens.
Ded Moroz (Grandfather Frost) came in red mittens.

related.en: gloves — with separate fingers: ordinary, leather, work, boxing
mittens — knitted, with a single thumb and no separate fingers
mittens, mitts — thick, without separate fingers, often work gloves; sounds old-fashioned

note: Boxing gloves are «боксёрские перча́тки», not рукави́цы.

examples.en: The bishop moves only diagonally.
He put his rook on the open file.
I lost my queen and lost the game.
The knight moves in an L shape.

related.en: queen — the strongest piece
rook — moves along straight lines; ладья́ is also an old word for a boat
bishop — moves diagonally; слон is also the animal, an elephant
knight — moves in an L shape; конь is also a horse

note: Do not translate these literally: слон («elephant») is the bishop, конь («horse») is the knight, ладья́ is the rook. King and pawn are the plain ones: коро́ль, пе́шка.

examples.ru: Для теста нужны мука, вода и [дро́жжи].
examples.en: Dough needs flour, water and yeast.

examples.ru: Летом в жару хорошо выпить холодного [ква́са].
examples.en: In the summer heat it's nice to drink cold kvass.

related.en: yeast — for dough, bread and beer (plural only)
kvass — a refreshing drink made from rye bread; not yeast

note: Дро́жжи is plural only: све́жие дро́жжи (fresh yeast), сухи́е дро́жжи (dry yeast).

examples.en: First whisk the eggs with the sugar.

examples.ru: Не [мути́] воду, я хочу видеть дно.
examples.en: Don't muddy the water, I want to see the bottom.

related.en: to make cloudy, to muddy: мути́ть во́ду; меня́ мути́т - I feel sick
to whisk, beat — eggs, cream: взбить яйца́

note: To whisk eggs or cream, use взбить, not мутить.

examples.en: She's in a good mood today.

examples.ru: Мне не нравится [расположе́ние] комнат в этой квартире.
examples.en: I don't like the layout of the rooms in this apartment.
He won his boss's favor.

related.en: mood — хорошее настроение
layout, location (of rooms, buildings); also favor, goodwill: добиться расположения

note: «Not in the mood» is нет настрое́ния.

examples.ru: В музее висит большая [карти́на] с морем.
examples.en: A big painting of the sea hangs in the museum.
My son brought a drawing home from school.
Send me your photo.

related.en: painting — a picture as a work of art, e.g. oil on canvas
drawing — in pencil, marker or crayons; also a pattern on fabric
photograph — a picture taken with a camera or phone

note: The verb depends on the tool: фотографи́ровать with a camera, рисова́ть with a pencil, писа́ть карти́ну (literally «to write») with paints.

examples.en: Turn on the speaker, let's listen to some music.

examples.ru: В телефоне сломался [дина́мик], я ничего не слышу.
examples.en: The speaker in my phone is broken, I can't hear anything.
The tourists walked in a column along the embankment.

related.en: speaker — a standalone one; also a newspaper column, and a gas pump
speaker — built into a phone, laptop or car
column, pillar; also a column of people or vehicles

note: A standalone speaker is коло́нка; the one inside a phone is дина́мик.

examples.en: Spread a clean cloth on the table.
It's time to change the baby's diaper.
The baby was dressed in a little shirt and rompers.

related.en: cloth diaper, flat baby cloth — the baby is wrapped in it or it is laid under him
disposable diaper, Pampers — goes on the baby's bottom
baby's shirt, undershirt — opens at the front

note: English «diaper» covers both cloth and disposable; Russian tells them apart. So «change the diaper» is usually поменя́ть подгу́зник, not пелёнку.

examples.ru: В июле в городе стоит страшная [жара́].
examples.en: There's terrible heat in the city in July.
He spoke with great passion.
The child has a fever, we need to call a doctor.

related.en: heat — intense hot weather outside — Любите жару́?
heat, glow; embers; figuratively fervor; also a sick person's fever

note: They are not the same word: жара́ is feminine (gen. жары́), жар is masculine (gen. жа́ра). A sick person's fever is often жар.

examples.en: Add a pinch of black pepper to the soup.

examples.ru: В салат я кладу помидоры и сладкий [пе́рец].
examples.en: I put tomatoes and sweet pepper in the salad.
Sprinkle the meat with paprika.

related.en: pepper — on its own, black pepper; with an adjective also the vegetable — чёрный пе́рец (black pepper), болга́рский пе́рец (bell pepper), о́стрый пе́рец (hot pepper)
paprika — mainly the ground spice; the vegetable is usually called болга́рский пе́рец

note: A bell pepper (the vegetable) is болга́рский пе́рец. The word пе́рец alone can mean several things, so the adjective decides which is meant.

examples.en: Slice the cheese and put it on the bread.

examples.ru: На завтрак я ем [творо́г] со сметаной.
examples.en: For breakfast I eat tvorog with sour cream.
You need fresh tvorog for syrniki.

related.en: cheese — firm or semi-hard, aged: on bread, in a sandwich
tvorog, cottage cheese — fresh, crumbly curd cheese, for breakfast, syrniki, pies

note: Сы́рники (cheese pancakes) are made from творо́г, not сыр.

examples.ru: На завтрак мама пожарила [блины́] с джемом.
examples.en: For breakfast Mom fried crepes with jam.
I like oladyi with sour cream.

related.en: blin — a thin crepe-like pancake, poured over the whole pan, often folded or filled
oladya — a small thick pancake, like an American pancake, from kefir or sour milk batter spooned into the pan

note: Batter spooned into the pan that turns out small and thick makes ола́дьи. Блины́ are thin, like crepes.

examples.en: The pot is on the stove.
Put the soup on the small burner.
The pie is still in the oven.

related.en: stove, cooker — the whole appliance (gas, electric) — кухо́нная плита́
burner — one ring on the stove
oven — the baking compartment of the stove

note: A pot goes на плиту́ or на конфо́рку, a pie goes в духо́вку.

meanings: уживаться, наслаждаться, получать удовольствие or кайфовать?

examples.en: The cat doesn't get along with the dog.

examples.ru: Мы весь день [наслажда́лись] морем и тишиной.
examples.en: We enjoyed the sea and the quiet all day.
I enjoy this music.
Yesterday we chilled out on the beach and really enjoyed ourselves.

related.en: to get along, live in harmony — уживаться с соседом
to enjoy, delight in something (+ instr.) — наслаждаться музыкой
to enjoy, take pleasure in (от + gen.) — получать удовольствие от работы
to enjoy oneself, chill (colloq.) — кайфовать на море

note: Ужива́ться means «to get along with someone», not «to enjoy». The other three are the verbs for «to enjoy».

examples.en: There was cherry kisel, a thick sweet fruit drink, for dessert.
In the morning I drink prostokvasha, soured milk, with bread.
Ryazhenka is made from baked milk.

related.en: kisel — a thick sweet drink of fruit juice and starch, warm or cold — клюквенный кисель
prostokvasha — soured milk, a bit like thin yogurt — стакан простокваши
ryazhenka — fermented baked milk with a mild caramel taste — ряженка с булочкой

note: Кисе́ль is not sour at all: it is sweet and thick.

examples.en: My daughter is in fifth grade.
He was admitted to the surgical department.

related.en: class, grade; the pupils of one grade; also a classroom — учи́ться в пя́том кла́ссе
department, section or branch of an institution — отделе́ние по́чты, поли́ции, больни́цы

note: A pupil is asked «в како́м ты кла́ссе?»; the answer is a number and a letter, e.g. в пя́том «Б».

examples.en: She put red lipstick on her lips.
Put ointment on the burn, it will heal quickly.

examples.ru: Купи [крем] для рук, у меня кожа сухая.
examples.en: Buy some hand cream, my skin is dry.

related.en: lipstick — губна́я пома́да; also hair pomade
ointment, salve — medicinal: мазь от ожо́гов
cream — skin cream; also the cream filling of a cake — крем для лица́

note: Пома́да is only for lips and hair; a medicinal ointment is мазь.

examples.en: She is Russian but lives in Belgrade.

examples.ru: У него [росси́йский] паспорт, хотя он татарин.
examples.en: He has a Russian passport, although he is a Tatar.

related.en: Russian by ethnicity and language — ру́сский язы́к, ру́сская культу́ра
Russian by state, of Russia — росси́йский паспорт, росси́йские зако́ны

note: English «Russian» covers both. A citizen of Russia is a россия́нин even if not ру́сский, for example a Tatar or a Chechen.

examples.en: I'm walking to the store.
Tomorrow we're going to Moscow.

related.en: to go on foot
to go by transport: car, train, bus

note:
English «to go» corresponds to two Russian verbs:
• идти́ - on foot
• е́хать - by any kind of transport

So «I'm going to Belgrade» by train is я е́ду в Белгра́д, not я иду́ в Белгра́д.

The same goes for ходи́ть and е́здить: «I travel often» is я ча́сто е́зжу.
title: Going in Russian: идти or ехать

examples.en: He is a doctor.
We are at home.

related.en: to be; left out in the present tense

note:
Russian has no verb быть («is», «am», «are») in the present tense, so the sentence goes without it.

• Он врач. - He is a doctor.
• Где ты? - Where are you?
• Мы до́ма. - We are at home.
• Э́то кни́га. - This is a book.

The verb comes back only in the past and the future: он был врачо́м, он бу́дет врачо́м.

Between two nouns a dash often stands in writing: Москва́ - столи́ца Росси́и.
title: Russian has no «is» in the present tense
